chapter: Band personalities, Duke's last years and the office
title: John Celley, Al's older brother
summary: John was nice, had little to do with the band, married a rich woman and died of heart trouble.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: How about John Kelley? Al's brother?
Well, John Kelley was -- I didn't know much about John; he was a nice fellow so far as I was concerned, but he had nothing to do with the band, you might as well say, you know?
We get a Christmas card from him every year.
John died.
We got one every year, I say. When he was alive.
John die?
Yeah.
Yeah, you know, he married a wealthy woman in Las Vegas.
Yeah, I saw him when my husband and I were in Las Vegas. We called, and John came out and took us to dinner.
What happened to him?
You know, he had heart trouble.

He had heart trouble for years. He died about -- Louie Bellson told me, about two years ago; Louie said that John died finally of a heart attack, but he was way up there in age; he was a lot older than Al.
Yeah, he was the older of the two.
Yeah, there were a lot of years between them, though. He was much older.
Al Kelley wasn't an old man.
Oh, no. John was what -- 15 or more years older than Al.
Yeah. He was a nice guy, too.
John? Oh, John had so much personality. Yeah, John was a very nice man.
Yeah ...
Didn't he work for Pearl and Louie for a while?
John Cello?
Yeah.
I don't think so.
I thought he did.
I don't know; I don't remember.
Well, what could he do?
Road manager. When Pearl was on tour, and Louie was playing.
Oh yeah, that's right.
But when Al used to take off, John would come in and substitute for him with Duke. You know, every once in awhile.
Yeah, I know.
So it seems to me that he worked for Pearl and Louie when they had a show on the road.
Maybe he did.
